title: Pitch of Sounds
keyIdea: Every sound is made by something vibrating. Pitch is how high or low a sound is, and it depends on how fast the object vibrates: faster vibrations make a higher pitch. Short, thin, tight or small objects vibrate faster, so they sound higher; long, thick, loose or big ones sound lower. Loudness is different: bigger vibrations make a louder sound at the same pitch.

kid: Hold a ruler on a table and twang the end. It wobbles up and down very fast. That is a vibration. All sounds are made by things that vibrate.
Pitch is how high or low a sound is. A whistle is high. A big drum is low. When something vibrates faster, its pitch is higher.
Make the ruler stick out less and twang it again. It vibrates faster, and the note goes up. A thin, tight elastic band sounds higher than a thick, loose one.
Loud is not the same as high. Hit a drum harder and it gets louder, but the note stays the same. Only faster or slower vibrations change the pitch.
adult: In England, Year 4 science asks children to say how sounds are made, linking them to something that vibrates. They look for patterns between the pitch of a sound and the object that made it. They also look for patterns between volume and the strength of the vibrations.

The key words are vibration, pitch, high, low, volume and loud. Pitch depends on the frequency: how many vibrations there are each second. Short rulers, thin or tight bands, small drums and short columns of air all vibrate faster. Volume depends on how big the vibrations are, not how fast.

Common mistakes to watch for: treating high as loud and low as quiet; thinking a thick or big object makes a higher note; and thinking a sound can happen with nothing vibrating. Bottles also cause muddles. Blow across one with more water and the note is higher, as the air column is shorter. Tap it and the note is lower.

In the lab your child twangs a ruler at four lengths and tunes an elastic band to its highest note. They put the notes of four bottles in order and hit a drum softly and hard, to see that loudness changes but pitch does not. Then they sort objects into high or low pitch.

familyTip: Stretch elastic bands of different thickness over an open box and pluck them. Which is highest? Then twang a ruler on the table edge, making it stick out less each time. Ask: did the note go up or down? Did it vibrate faster or slower? Finish by humming high and low with a hand on your throat.

visual.caption: High pitch or low pitch? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: twang a ruler, tune an elastic band, order bottle notes, hit a drum soft and hard, and sort high and low.

practice.prompt: Ruler A sticks out {a} cm over the table. Ruler B sticks out {=a+d} cm. You twang both. Which note is higher?
practice.hint: Which one will vibrate faster: the short end or the long end?
practice.explain: Ruler A sticks out less, so it vibrates faster. Faster vibrations make a higher pitch.

practice.prompt: Bottle A has {a} cm of water. Bottle B has {=a+d} cm of water. You blow across the tops. Which note is higher?
practice.hint: When you blow, the air vibrates. Which bottle has the shorter column of air?
practice.explain: Bottle B has more water, so less air above it. A shorter column of air vibrates faster and gives a higher note.

practice.hint: Put your hand on your throat and hum. What do you feel?
practice.explain: All sounds are made by vibrations. When you hum, your vocal cords vibrate and you can feel the buzz.

practice.prompt: Ali hits a drum harder. What changes?
practice.hint: Hitting harder makes the vibrations bigger. Does that change the speed or the size?
practice.explain: A harder hit makes bigger vibrations, so the sound is louder. The pitch stays the same.

pool.prompt: Maya turns the peg on her guitar {n} times to make the string tighter. What happens to the note?
pool.hint: Does a tighter string vibrate faster or slower?
pool.explain: A tighter string vibrates faster, so the note gets higher. That is how a guitar is tuned.

pool.prompt: Drum A is {a} cm across. Drum B is {=a+d} cm across. Their skins are just as tight. Which sounds higher?
pool.hint: Small things vibrate faster than big things.
pool.explain: Drum A is smaller, so its skin vibrates faster and makes a higher note. Big drums sound lower.

pool.prompt: Which elastic band makes the lowest note?
pool.hint: Thick and loose both make the vibrations slower.
pool.explain: A thick, loose band vibrates slowest, so it has the lowest pitch. Thin and tight bands sound higher.

pool.prompt: Sam says a high sound is always a loud sound. Is he right?
choices: No, pitch and loudness are different
pool.hint: Can you sing a high note very quietly?
pool.explain: No. Pitch depends on how fast something vibrates. Loudness depends on how big the vibrations are.

pool.hint: Think of the short ruler twang.
pool.explain: Faster vibrations make a higher pitch. Slower vibrations make a lower pitch.

pool.prompt: On a xylophone, which bars make the high notes?
pool.explain: The short bars vibrate faster, so they make the high notes. The long bars make the low notes.

pool.prompt: Two bottles have the same amount of water. You blow gently across one and hard across the other. What is different?
pool.hint: The air column is the same length in both. What does blowing harder change?
pool.explain: Same water means the same column of air, so the same pitch. Blowing harder makes it louder.

pool.prompt: Your twanged ruler makes a low note. How can you make it higher?
pool.explain: Make it stick out less. A shorter end vibrates faster and gives a higher note. Twanging gently only makes it quieter.
